summary: Carl Friedrich Gauss studied at Collegium Carolinum (1792–1795), the University of Göttingen (1795–1798), and the University of Helmstedt (~1798–1799). He held a post at the University of Göttingen from ~1807 to 1855.
Carl Gaedicke, who worked in Indology and linguistics, earned his PhD at the University of Jena in 1877. He studied under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Olson works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Mentored by John Y. Fenton, he held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College, attested between 2005 and 2015.

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, also studying under Sonam Germano, William Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried studied Indology and religious studies at Halle-Wittenberg (~1849–1852) and Bonn (~1852–1853), under Albrecht Weber (1849) and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Schulpforta (~1865–1875), Jena (~1875–1903), and Trinity College Dublin as Professor of Sanskrit.

Carl W. Ernst works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Stanford University (~1968–1973) and Harvard University (~1973–1981), later serving as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill from 1992 to 2022.
Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Groningen from 1908 to 1916 and Utrecht University from 1917 to 1946.
Carlo Giussani worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) and under Giuseppe Bardelli, Albrecht Weber (1863), and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1866).
Carlo Jamelle Harris studied philosophy and Buddhist studies at National Chengchi University, where he earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin.

Carmen Blacker studied Japanology and religious studies at Somerville College (~1947–1951) and under Shigeru Gorai (~1961–1963). She served as a Lecturer in Japanese at the University of Cambridge from ~1955 to 1991.

Carmen Dragonetti studied at the National University of San Marcos (~1964–1969). She was a fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (1989), a visiting scholar at Nyingma Institute (1996), and served as vice director at Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (attested 2001).

Carmen Meinert completed her PhD at the University of Bonn in 2001. A specialist in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology, she has held posts as a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and Ruhr University Bochum.

Carol S. Anderson works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College.

Carola Roloff earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1998–2009) under David P. Jackson in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She held posts at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg and as a researcher at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2006–2007).
Carola S. Carstens, a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned her doctorate at the University of Hamburg by 2005 and held a post at Rice University from 1998 to 1999.

Carole McGranahan studied at Colgate University and the University of Michigan (PhD 2001) under Nicholas B. Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler. A scholar in Tibetology and archaeology, she was an Assistant Professor of Anthropology at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2001–2008).

Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids studied at University College London (~1886–1889) under Thomas William Rhys Davids (~1889–1894). She lectured at the University of Manchester (~1904–1910) and SOAS (~1918–1942), and served as President of the Pali Text Society (~1923–1942).

Caroline Humphrey studied at Girton College, Cambridge (~1962–1966) and under Edmund Leach (~1968–1973). Specializing in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies, she held posts at Michigan, the Scott Polar Research Institute, Cambridge (~1978), and King's College (~1978).

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt earned her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 1990). Working in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, she was a Graduate Teaching Associate at Ohio State and a Visiting Lecturer at Denison University (attested 1990).
Carson Schütze studied linguistics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1997.
